algorithm: Construct a simple undirected graph from the input vertices and edges
For each vertex v in the graph, compute the shortest path distances to all other vertices
Determine the maximum distance from v to any other vertex as the eccentricity of v
Return a dictionary mapping each vertex to its eccentricity
constraints: Graph must be simple (no self-loops or multiple edges)
Eccentricity is defined for all vertices in the graph
Output must be a dictionary with string keys and integer values
edge_cases: n=1: single vertex with no edges (eccentricity 0)
Graph with isolated vertices: include in eccentricity calculation
Graph with multiple connected components: raise ValueError
inputs: n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n
output: Dictionary with string keys (vertex names) mapping to integers (eccentricity values). If the graph is disconnected, raise ValueError.
purpose: Compute the eccentricity of each node in a simple undirected unweighted graph with n vertices (0 to n-1) and given edges. Eccentricity of a node is the maximum shortest path distance from that node to any other node in the graph.
